data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The panel is an aggregate, so error clustering must be measured as inter-rater agreement on failure cases, not just the presence of a single failure.","The expert's 'holistic intuition' is a black box, making the comparison of error structures more difficult than comparing two explicit models."],"overturn_conditions":["The expert also fails systematically on the same cases, suggesting the omitted features are not causally relevant.","The inter-rater agreement on failure cases is low, suggesting non-experts are using unlisted features, contradicting the 'compliance' assumption."],"shared_structure":["Distinguishing between a genuine mechanism and a spurious correlation requires examining the structure of errors, not just aggregate accuracy.","Error clustering on omitted variables is a signature of model incompleteness."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["Inter-rater agreement on cases where the panel is wrong indicates that the checklist is driving the error, not individual non-expert noise.","If the expert succeeds on these clustered-error cases, it proves the checklist is incomplete and the reliability gain is merely compliance with an incomplete proxy.","Genuine reliability gain requires that the panel's errors be uncorrelated with the features the expert uses to succeed."]},"claim":"The non-expert panel will only produce a genuine reliability gain if the checklist is causally complete (captures all necessary and sufficient features); evidence within a single evaluation distinguishing this from mere compliance is the presence of correlated errors on cases where the checklist is silent. If the panel's errors cluster on unchecklisted features, the gain is mere compliance tracking the right answer only where the checklist is informative.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The expert's intuition is also anchored to the same incomplete set of features as the checklist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is already causally complete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The unchecklisted features are perceptually invisible to non-experts but causally inert, so they do not affect the outcome.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A checklist operationalizes an incomplete subset of the causal features determining the outcome. Non-experts will exhibit high inter-rater reliability (agreement) but low external validity (accuracy) on cases where the unlisted features dominate. The expert, relying on a holistic intuition, will not exhibit this clustered error signature because their implicit model can incorporate unlisted features. Genuine reliability gain implies the checklist is causally sufficient, so no such error cluster should exist; mere compliance implies the error cluster will be present and highly correlated across panelists.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
